review_notes: I read the whole file. I also grepped the lean directory for uses of the unscaled and scaled approach lemmas. The unscaled lemmas `sle_high_center_approach`, `sle_low_center_approach` and `sle_annular_small_target` are only used by each other, at lines 297 and 303. Only the `_scaled` variants are used downstream, at line 542. The `_scaled` versions are line-by-line generalizations of the unscaled ones with `R` inserted, and the unscaled statements are the `R = 1` instances. The other candidates are small. Examples are the `hd` distance computation and `let : IsProbabilityMeasure`, which are routine. The `hsβ` and `hid` sqrt-power identities are short. I did not report these. The proposed rewrites have not been compiled. They depend on `simpa`/`one_mul` normalising `1 * r` and `1 / 2`, which I did not check.

findings.declaration: sle_high_center_approach / sle_low_center_approach / sle_annular_small_target (duplicated by their `_scaled` versions)
findings.problem: Three long proofs are re-done almost verbatim for general R in `sle_high_center_approach_scaled` (322–354), `sle_low_center_approach_scaled` (366–417) and `sle_annular_small_target_scaled` (421–447). This includes the visit-bound exponent cancellation, the projection to the real-axis point z.re with `hd`, `hx`, `hx0`, `he`, `hq` and `hsβ`, and the min-exponent / constant comparison case split. The unscaled lemmas are exactly the R = 1 instances: the hypotheses 1/2 ≤ ‖z‖ and ‖z‖ ≤ 2 are R/2 ≤ ‖z‖ and ‖z‖ ≤ 2R at R = 1, and the radius `r` is `1*r`. Nothing outside these six declarations uses the unscaled versions; the only later use is the scaled `sle_annular_small_target_scaled` at line 542. Every non-trivial estimate is therefore maintained twice, and a fix to one copy must be mirrored in the other.
findings.proposed_change: Move the scaled section (322–447) before the unscaled one, or delete the unscaled versions. If the unscaled names are wanted as API, restate them as one-line corollaries of the scaled lemmas at R = 1. For example, `sle_high_center_approach` is `by simpa using sle_high_center_approach_scaled κ hκ hκ8 γ hSLE z 1 r one_pos hr (by simpa using hy)`. `sle_low_center_approach` is `by simpa using sle_low_center_approach_scaled κ hκ hκ8 γ hSLE z 1 one_pos hz (by simpa using hn) r hr hr16 (by simpa using hy)`. `sle_annular_small_target` is `by simpa using sle_annular_small_target_scaled κ hκ hκ8 γ hSLE z 1 one_pos hz (by simpa using hn) (by simpa using _hn2) r hr hr16`. The hypotheses stay as stated: `Real.sqrt r ≤ z.im`, `1/2 ≤ ‖z‖`, `‖z‖ ≤ 2` and `z.im ≤ Real.sqrt r`. The only rewriting needed is `one_mul` and `1/2 = 1/2`-style normalisation, with `R = 1` after `one_mul`.
findings.benefit: This removes roughly 130 lines of duplicated analytic proof (the `hd`/`hx`/`hq` real-axis projection argument and the exponent algebra). It leaves one proof of each estimate, so a reader sees that the unscaled and scaled versions are the same fact. The scaled lemmas are the ones actually used downstream, so maintenance effort goes where it matters.
